predecessors.name: Naiman
predecessors.text: the western Mongolian steppe of the Naiman, absorbed before 1206

predecessors.name: Kerait
predecessors.text: the Keraite steppe of central Mongolia

predecessors.name: Merkit
predecessors.text: the Merkit lands on the Selenga

predecessors.name: Yenisei Kyrgyz
predecessors.text: the Yenisei Kyrgyz row (1206 shape), whose dossier ends in 1208

successors.name: Yuan dynasty
successors.text: China, Mongolia and the east under Kublai's line

successors.name: Golden Horde
successors.text: the Jochid ulus: Kipchak steppe, Volga, Rus' as tributaries

successors.name: Ilkhanate

successors.name: Chagatai Khanate
successors.text: Transoxiana, Semirechye and the Tarim under Chagatai's line

ledger.x: 1206: a kurultai proclaims Temüjin khan and the Mongol Empire begins on the Mongolian Plateau.
1208: the Yenisei Kyrgyz submit.
1207-1208: Jochi subjugates the Siberian forest peoples.
1209: the Western Xia are subjugated.
1209: the Uyghurs of Qocho join.
1211: the Mongols invade the Jin.
1 June 1215: Zhongdu, the Jin Central Capital, falls.
1216: Jebe is sent after Kuchlug.
1218: Xinjiang is Mongol and Kuchlug is dead.
1219: the Mongols invade Khwarazmia.
1220: the Qara Khitai contest closes.
1220: the Qara Khitai core passes to the Mongols: 'The Mongols fully conquered the former territories of the Qara-Khitai in 1220' (Qara Khitai page).
1220: the Irtysh and the Altai edge are inside the Mongol shape (798 of the 804 cells of kimek's 1216-1220 step).
1221: the Khwarazmian war ends in a Mongol Central Asia.
1221: the Khwarazmian lands pass to the Mongols.
1223: the northern Jin provinces are cleared.
1223: Shanxi, Hebei and Shandong are Mongol.
1227: the Western Xia are destroyed.
1227: the Western Xia land becomes Mongol.
1227: the Kazakh steppe, the Aral steppe and the Urals are inside the Mongol shape (all 4,901 cells of kimek's 1220-1227 step).
1230: Ögedei takes the field against the Jin.
26 August 1231: the Mongols invade Goryeo.
August 1231: the Khwarazmian rump passes to the Mongols.
1233: Guyuk conquers the Eastern Xia.
9 February 1234: the Jin dynasty ends at Caizhou.
9 February 1234: North China is annexed.
1235: Karakorum becomes the capital.
1236: Batu's armies take the Kipchak steppe west of the Urals.
1236: Volga Bulgaria is Mongol.
1237: the Mongols attack Principality of Ryazan.
1237: Principality of Ryazan is taken.
1237: Principality of Ryazan becomes a Mongol vassal.
1238: the Mongols attack Cumania.
1238: the Mongols attack Principality of Rostov-Suzdal.
1238: Principality of Rostov-Suzdal is taken.
1238: Principality of Rostov-Suzdal becomes a Mongol vassal.
1239: the Mongols attack Principality of Pereyaslavl.
1239: Principality of Pereyaslavl is taken.
1239: Principality of Pereyaslavl becomes a Mongol vassal.
1239: the Mongols attack Principality of Chernigov.
1239: Principality of Chernigov is taken.
1239: Principality of Chernigov becomes a Mongol vassal.
November 1239: the siege of Maghas opens.
February 1240: Maghas falls.
February 1240: the Alan land passes to the Mongols.
1240: the Mongols attack Principality of Kiev.
1240: Principality of Kiev is taken.
1240: Principality of Kiev becomes a Mongol vassal.
1240: the Mongols attack Principality of Galicia-Volhynia.
1240: Principality of Galicia-Volhynia is taken.
1240: Principality of Galicia-Volhynia becomes a Mongol vassal.
1240: the Mongols attack Halych-Volhynia occupation.
1240: Halych-Volhynia occupation is taken.
1240: Halych-Volhynia occupation becomes a Mongol vassal.
1241: Cuman control of the Pontic steppes ends.
1241: the Pontic steppe passes to the Mongols.
1241: Turov and Pinsk are inside the Mongol shape (295 of 297 cells; the Cliopatria row ends in 1240).
1241: Smolensk is inside the Mongol shape from 1241 to 1293 (521 of 522 cells of its 1236-1240 shape); Cliopatria's Smolensk row has no shape between 1241 and 1293.

1241: Novgorod and Pskov land is inside the Mongol shape from 1241 to 1284 (910 cells of the Novgorod and Pskov shapes of 1285 in 1241, 965 from 1250): Cliopatria's Novgorod Republic row has no shape between 1241 and 1284, and the shape drops the land in 1285 when the row resumes.
1241: Chengdu.
11 April 1241: the Hungarian army is destroyed at Mohi.
1242: the Mongols withdraw from Central Europe.
1243: the Sultanate of Rum becomes a Mongol client.
1243: Georgia acknowledges the Great Khan as overlord.
1250: Tibet is Mongol (the year is the step in the Cliopatria shape: Tibet 1,093 cells in 1241, 7,065 in 1250).
1250: eastern Anatolia (Erzurum, Sivas and the east of the Rum row's 1241 shape) enters the Mongol shape (Anatolia region: 29 cells in 1241, 1,215 in 1250).
1253: the Dali Kingdom submits.
1257: the Ismaili strongholds fall.
1258: Baghdad falls and the Abbasid Caliphate ends.
1258: the Mongols create Ssangseong Prefecture in the north-east.
1258: the Mongols take Thăng Long.

1258: 'Uriyangkhadai left Thang Long after nine days to invade the Song dynasty'; 'One month after fleeing the capital in 1258, Trần Thái Tông returned and commenced regular diplomatic relations' and a 'tributary relationship with the Mongol court'.
Spring 1259: peace with Goryeo.
1259: Goryeo becomes a Mongol client.
1260: Yunnan is drawn as direct Mongol land.

1260: the Dali land is annexed (bridge as above; the Dali page's infobox says 'Conquered by the Mongol Empire: 1253' and History of Yunnan 'destroyed by an invasion of the Mongol Empire' in 1253, but the Duan rulers stayed as tusi chiefs and the province dates from 1274).
1260: the Toluid Civil War begins between Kublai and his brother Ariq Böke.
1260: the rest of Sichuan enters the Mongol shape (Sichuan 719 of 1,987 cells in 1250, 1,699 in 1260).
January 1260: Hulagu's army takes Aleppo and then Damascus.
September-October 1260: the Mongols lose Syria.
1264: Ariq Böke surrenders at Shangdu and the Toluid Civil War ends.
1270: the Mongols create Dongnyeong Prefecture in the north-west.
1271: Karakorum ends as capital and Khanbaliq follows.
18 December 1271: Kublai gives the empire a Han-style dynastic name.
1276: the Song imperial family surrenders.
1279: the Song dynasty is defeated.
February 1283: Sogetu's fleet lands in Champa.
December 1283: the Mongols break into the Pagan frontier.
5 February 1284: Tagaung falls.
February 1284: northern Burma to Tagaung is Mongol.
February 1285: the Yuan take Thăng Long.
June 1285: the Mongols leave Champa.
9 June 1285: 'Mongol troops evacuated Thăng Long to withdraw to China.'
February 1288: Toghon's Yuan army returns to Thăng Long ('In October 1287, the Yuan land forces commanded by Toghon' began moving south; 'Toghon returned to the capital Thăng Long to loot food').
5 March 1288: the Yuan 'retreated from Thăng Long to their fortified main base in Vạn Kiếp northeast of Hanoi on 5 March 1288'; their fleet was ambushed at the Bạch Đằng River in April 1288.
1290: Dongnyeong returns to Goryeo.
1293: the nominal empire ends; four khanates follow from 1294.

wars.name: Mongol conquest of the Western Xia
wars.outcome: The Western Xia were subjugated in 1209 and destroyed in 1227.

wars.name: Mongol–Jin War
wars.outcome: Zhongdu fell on 1 June 1215, the Jin moved the capital to Kaifeng in 1214 and ended at Caizhou on 9 February 1234; North China was annexed.

wars.name: Mongol conquest of the Qara Khitai
wars.outcome: Jebe defeated the Qara Khitai at Balasaghun in 1216; Kuchlug was killed in 1218; the Mongols held all of Xinjiang by 1218.

wars.name: Mongol invasion of Khwarazmia
wars.outcome: After the Otrar incident of 1218 the Mongols took 'all the territories of the former Khwarazmian Empire' by 1221.

wars.name: Mongol invasions of Korea
wars.outcome: Saritai crossed the Yalu on 26 August 1231; Mongol darughachis controlled almost all of North Pyongan from 1232; a peace agreement was concluded in the spring of 1259 and Goryeo became a vassal; the Mongols kept Ssangseong Prefecture (from 1258) and…

wars.name: Mongol invasion of Europe
wars.outcome: Ryazan fell in December 1237, Yuri was killed on 4 March 1238, Kiev was sacked on 6 December 1240; Hungary was beaten at Mohi (11 April 1241) and evacuated by mid-1242.

wars.name: Mongol conquest of the Song dynasty
wars.outcome: The Song recaptured Siyang-yang in 1239; the imperial family surrendered in 1276 and the Song were defeated in 1279.

wars.name: Mongol conquest of the Dali Kingdom
wars.outcome: King Duan Xingzhi defected and Dali became a vassal state in 1253.

wars.name: Hulagu's campaign against the Nizari Ismailis
wars.outcome: The strongholds were destroyed in 1257 except Girdkuh, which held out until 1271.

wars.name: Siege of Baghdad
wars.outcome: Baghdad was captured and sacked in 1258.

wars.name: Mongol invasion of Đại Việt (first, 1258)
wars.outcome: Uriyangkhadai entered Đại Việt via Yunnan in early 1258, beat the Viet on 17 January 1258 and occupied Thăng Long for nine days before leaving for the Song; Trần Thái Tông returned a month later and opened a tributary relationship with the Mongol court.

wars.name: Mongol-Mamluk war (Ain Jalut)
wars.outcome: The Mongols took Aleppo (January 1260) and Damascus (1 March 1260) and held northern Syria for about eight months; the Mamluks 'decisively halt[ed] their advance for the first time' at Ain Jalut on 3 September 1260, 'captured Damascus five days later ...…

wars.name: Toluid Civil War
wars.outcome: Kublai prevailed; Ariq Böke surrendered at Shangdu in 1264.

wars.name: Mongol invasions of Japan
wars.outcome: 'In 1274 and again in 1281, Kublai Khan invaded Japan on two separate occasions'; no land was gained.

wars.name: Mongol invasions of Burma
wars.outcome: The Mongols won the Vochang valley in April 1277 and, after the invasion that 'began on 22 September 1283', took Tagaung on 5 February 1284 and held northern Burma to Tagaung as the province of Zhengmian until 4 April 1303; Pagan itself was not annexed.

wars.name: Mongol invasion of Champa
wars.outcome: Sogetu's fleet landed near Thị Nại Bay in February 1283 and took Vijaya two days later; the Mongols held it until they were repelled in June 1285 and Sogetu was killed at Chương Dương.

wars.name: Mongol invasions of Đại Việt
wars.outcome: The Yuan took Thăng Long in February 1285 and left on 9 June 1285, returned in February 1288 and retreated to Vạn Kiếp on 5 March 1288; their fleet was ambushed at the Bạch Đằng River in April 1288.

certainty.note: Steppe, desert and mountain frontiers and nominal suzerainty over four uluses: no treaty or survey lines.
